notes: The distributive ish ish is rendered once: the first occurrence carries Whosoever he, the second is unrepresented under rule 22. The competing reading fuses the pair under rule 30's one-English-word condition, which the unit note records.

Both assimilated articles (before Molech, before stones) are unrepresented; the article on ha-arets takes the written the standing before its own word under rule 29's arthrous count, with the construct taking the supplied one.
The prepositional predicate min carries the clause's copula under rule 49 (be of).
